6	import Mathlib

10	
11	/-!
12	# The Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
13	
14	This file states Milne's
15	*Abelian Varieties* §III.6 Proposition 6.1: for a complete nonsingular curve
16	`C` of genus `g > 0` over an algebraically closed field `k̄` and a marked
17	`k̄`-point `P₀ ∈ C(k̄)`, the Abel–Jacobi morphism
18	`ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` is the **Albanese morphism** of the pointed curve
19	`(C, P₀)`: any pointed morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety with
20	`φ(P₀) = η_A` factors uniquely as `φ = ψ ∘ ι_{P₀}` for a homomorphism of
21	group schemes `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`.
22	
23	The route taken is the **symmetric-power route** (cube-free): the
24	symmetric assignment `(P₁,…,P_g) ↦ φ(P₁) + ⋯ + φ(P_g)` factors through
25	`Sym^g C`, the resulting morphism `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` descends through
26	the birational morphism `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` to a rational map
27	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⇢ A`, and Milne's Theorem I.3.2 (`extend_to_av` in the sibling
28	`Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`, A.4.c) promotes it to a regular
29	morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`. The group-homomorphism property of `ψ` then
30	follows from `ψ(η_J) = η_A` together with Milne Corollary I.1.2 (a
31	consequence of `thm:rigidity_lemma`).
32	
33	## Main results
34	
35	* `Pic0.abelJacobi` — the regular morphism `ι_{P₀} : C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
36	  (`lem:abel_jacobi_morphism`).
37	* `Pic0.SymmetricPower` — the `g`-th symmetric power `Sym^g C` of the curve
38	  `C`, as a `k̄`-scheme (Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1).
39	* `Pic0.symmetricPowerAVMap` — the symmetrised morphism
40	  `Sym^g φ : Sym^g C ⟶ A` induced by a morphism `φ : C ⟶ A` into an abelian
41	  variety.
42	* `Pic0.symmetricPowerToJacobian` — the birational morphism
43	  `f^{(g)} : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`.
44	* `Pic0.descentThroughBirationalSigma` — the descent of `Sym^g φ` to a unique
45	  regular morphism `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A`, via Milne Theorem I.3.2.
46	* `Pic0.albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq` — the connecting biconditional:
47	  `φ = ι_{P₀} ≫ ψ` holds iff `Sym^g φ = f^{(g)} ≫ ψ`.
48	* `Pic0.albanese_universal_property` — the universal property itself (Milne
49	  Proposition III.6.1), assembled from the previous two.
50	
51	## Remaining obligations
52	
53	`albanese_universal_property` is assembled from
54	`descentThroughBirationalSigma` and `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq`, but
55	six declarations of this file are stated without proof:
56	
57	* `abelJacobi` — the moduli classifier of the rigidified diagonal
58	  correspondence `𝓛^{P₀} = 𝓞_{C × C}(Δ − {P₀} × C − C × {P₀})`, taken as a
59	  relative degree-zero line bundle over the second factor.
60	* `SymmetricPower` — the affine-and-glue construction `Spec(A^{⊗ g})^{S_g}`
61	  of Milne III.3 Proposition 3.1 (Mumford 1970 §II.7 / §III.11). Mathlib has
62	  no scheme-theoretic symmetric power, only `Sym` for types and modules.
63	* `symmetricPowerAVMap` and `symmetricPowerToJacobian` — the two invocations
64	  of the universal property of `Sym^g C`, which need the symmetric projection
65	  `π : C^g ⟶ Sym^g C` supplied by that construction.
66	* `descentThroughBirationalSigma` — extension of the rational map
67	  `Sym^g φ ∘ (f^{(g)})^{-1}` to a regular morphism (Milne Theorem I.3.2).
68	* `albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq` — Milne's identification of `ι_{P₀}`
69	  with `Q ↦ Q + (g − 1) P₀` followed by `f^{(g)}`.
70	
71	## The scheme `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
72	
73	`Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` is taken from `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` through a thin
74	`Pic0.Bundle` structure that carries the underlying scheme together with its
75	four abelian-variety attributes (`GrpObj`, `IsProper`, `Smooth`,
76	`GeometricallyIrreducible`), the carrier `Pic0.bundle C`, and the derived
77	definition `Pic0.jacobianScheme C := (bundle C).scheme`.
78	
79	The upstream declarations `Scheme.Pic0.{grpObj, proper, smooth,
80	geometricallyIrreducible}` run under `[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]`,
81	`[HasPicScheme C]` and `[PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]`, whereas
82	the Albanese curve enters carrying only smoothness, properness and geometric
83	irreducibility over `k̄`. The three bridges of §0.0
84	(`geometricallyReduced_of_smooth`, `GeometricallyIntegral.of_…`,
85	`hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed`) discharge the missing hypotheses over an
86	algebraically closed base.
87	
88	## Abelian-variety conventions
89	
90	Following the project (cf. `AbelianVarietyRigidity.lean`, `Jacobian.lean`),
91	an **abelian variety over `k̄`** is encoded as an object
92	`A : Over (Spec (.of k̄))` carrying the four instances:
93	
94	- `[GrpObj A]` (group-object structure on the over-category),
95	- `[IsProper A.hom]` (complete),
96	- `[Smooth A.hom]` (nonsingular),
97	- `[GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]` (geometrically irreducible).
98	
99	A **smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over `k̄`** carries:
100	
101	- `[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]`,
102	- `[IsProper C.hom]`,
103	- `[GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]`.
104	
105	These instances are supplied by `inferInstance` at the call site.
106	
107	## References
108	
109	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Albanese_AlbaneseUP.tex`.
110	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.6 Proposition 6.1, p. 104;
111	§III.3 Proposition 3.1 (symmetric power), p. 94; §III.5 Theorem 5.1(a)
112	(birationality of `f^{(g)}`), p. 101 (`references/abelian-varieties.pdf`).
113	-/

123	/-! ## §0.0. Substrate bridges: geometric integrality and rational points
124	
125	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` states `Pic⁰_{C/k}` smooth,
126	proper and geometrically irreducible under the hypotheses
127	`[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
128	[PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]`, whereas the Albanese curve `C`
129	enters here carrying only `[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
130	[GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]` over an algebraically closed field `k̄`. The
131	three bridging facts below discharge the missing hypotheses, so that
132	`Pic0.bundle` can be assembled from the upstream declarations. -/
133	
134	/-- **Reducedness descends along a faithfully flat morphism.** If `π : Y ⟶ X` is
135	flat and surjective (i.e. faithfully flat) and `Y` is reduced, then `X` is
136	reduced: each stalk map `𝒪_{X,π(y)} → 𝒪_{Y,y}` is a flat local homomorphism of
137	local rings, hence faithfully flat and in particular injective, so `𝒪_{X,π(y)}`
138	embeds into the reduced ring `𝒪_{Y,y}`. -/
139	theorem isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (π : Y ⟶ X)
140	    [Flat π] [Surjective π] [IsReduced Y] : IsReduced X := by
141	  haveI hst : ∀ x : X, _root_.IsReduced (X.presheaf.stalk x) := by
142	    intro x
143	    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := π.surjective x
144	    have hlocal : IsLocalHom (π.stalkMap y).hom := inferInstance
145	    have hflat : (π.stalkMap y).hom.Flat := Flat.stalkMap π y
146	    have hinj : Function.Injective (π.stalkMap y).hom := by
147	      algebraize [(π.stalkMap y).hom]
148	      haveI : Module.Flat (X.presheaf.stalk (π.base y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y) := hflat
149	      haveI : IsLocalHom (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk (π.base y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) := hlocal
150	      haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat (X.presheaf.stalk (π.base y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y) :=
151	        Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom
152	      exact FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective _ _
153	    exact isReduced_of_injective (π.stalkMap y).hom hinj
154	  exact isReduced_of_isReduced_stalk X
155	
156	/-- **A scheme smooth over an algebraically closed field is geometrically
157	reduced.** For each test field `K/k̄`, the base change `X ×_{k̄} K` is smooth
158	over `K`; its further base change to `K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K` is smooth over an
159	algebraically closed field, hence reduced
160	(`Scheme.isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed`), and reducedness descends along the
161	faithfully flat projection `X_{K̄} → X_K` (`isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective`). -/
162	theorem geometricallyReduced_of_smooth {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
163	    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of kbar)) [Smooth f] :
164	    GeometricallyReduced f := by
165	  refine ⟨?_⟩
166	  rw [geometrically_iff_of_commRing_of_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms]
167	  intro K _ _
168	  have hfsurj : (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))).hom.FaithfullyFlat :=
169	    RingHom.faithfullyFlat_algebraMap_iff.mpr inferInstance
170	  have hFS := (flat_and_surjective_SpecMap_iff
171	    (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))).mpr hfsurj
172	  haveI : Flat (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))) := hFS.1
173	  haveI : Surjective (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))) := hFS.2
174	  haveI hsm1 : Smooth (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K)))) :=
175	    inferInstance
176	  haveI hsm2 : Smooth (pullback.snd
177	      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
178	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))))) := inferInstance
179	  haveI : Smooth (Over.mk (pullback.snd
180	      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
181	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))))).hom := hsm2
182	  haveI : IsReduced (pullback (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
183	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))))) :=
184	    Scheme.isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed (kbar := AlgebraicClosure K) (Over.mk (pullback.snd
185	      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
186	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))))))
187	  exact isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective
188	    (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
189	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))))
190	
191	/-- **A smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over an algebraically closed
192	field has a rational point.** `C.left` is nonempty (geometric irreducibility over
193	the one-point base `Spec k̄`), locally of finite type over `k̄` (smoothness) and
194	therefore a Jacobson space, so it has a closed point `x`; over the algebraically
195	closed field `k̄`, `pointOfClosedPoint`/`pointEquivClosedPoint` promote `x` to a
196	`k̄`-rational section of `C.hom`. This discharges `[HasRationalPoint C]`. -/
197	theorem hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
198	    (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [Smooth C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
199	    Scheme.HasRationalPoint C := by
200	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom := inferInstance
201	  haveI : IrreducibleSpace C.left :=
202	    GeometricallyIrreducible.irreducibleSpace_of_subsingleton C.hom
203	  haveI : JacobsonSpace C.left := LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace C.hom
204	  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := nonempty_inter_closedPoints (X := C.left) (Z := Set.univ)
205	    Set.univ_nonempty isClosed_univ.isLocallyClosed
206	  exact ⟨⟨(pointEquivClosedPoint C.hom).symm ⟨x, hx.2⟩⟩⟩

208	namespace Pic0
209	
210	/-! ## §0. File-internal placeholder for `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`
211	
212	The identity component of the Picard scheme, together with its degree map, is
213	constructed in `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`. The helper below — a bundled
214	structure carrying the Pic⁰ scheme together with its four abelian-variety
215	instances, plus the carrier `bundle` — supplies the interface. `bundle` is
216	wired to the upstream declarations (`Scheme.Pic0Scheme`,
217	`Scheme.Pic0.{grpObj, proper, smooth, geometricallyIrreducible}`) through the
218	§0.0 bridges; the derived `jacobianScheme` def and the four typeclass carriers
219	below are projections from `bundle`. -/
220	
221	/-- Interface for `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`: bundles the underlying `k̄`-scheme together
222	with the four abelian-variety structural instances (group object, proper,
223	smooth, geometrically irreducible). -/
224	structure Bundle {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
225	    (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar)))
226	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
227	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] where
228	  /-- The underlying scheme `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`. -/
229	  scheme : Over (Spec (.of kbar))
230	  /-- Group-object structure on `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`. -/
231	  grpObj : GrpObj scheme
232	  /-- Properness of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` over `k̄`. -/
233	  proper : IsProper scheme.hom
234	  /-- Smoothness of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` over `k̄`. -/
235	  smooth : Smooth scheme.hom
236	  /-- Geometric irreducibility of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` over `k̄`. -/
237	  geomIrred : GeometricallyIrreducible scheme.hom
238	
239	variable {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
240	
241	variable (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar)))
242	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
243	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
244	
245	/-- **The `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` bundle.** For a smooth
246	proper geometrically irreducible curve `C` over an algebraically closed field
247	`k̄`, the underlying scheme is `Scheme.Pic0Scheme C` and its four
248	abelian-variety attributes are the identity-component theorems of
249	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` (`Scheme.Pic0.{grpObj, proper, smooth,
250	geometricallyIrreducible}`).
251	
252	The upstream declarations run under `[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]`,
253	`[HasPicScheme C]` and `[PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]`; over `k̄`
254	these are discharged honestly here:
255	`geometricallyReduced_of_smooth` + `GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom` give
256	`GeometricallyIntegral C.hom`; `hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed` gives
257	`[HasRationalPoint C]`, whence `instHasPicScheme` supplies `[HasPicScheme C]` and
258	`instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` the local-finiteness carrier. -/
259	noncomputable def bundle : Bundle C := by
260	  haveI : Smooth C.hom := SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth 1 C.hom
261	  haveI : GeometricallyReduced C.hom := geometricallyReduced_of_smooth C.hom

that the classical emptiness proof (Milne Lemma 3.3) is phrased with Weil divisors, and
Mathlib has no Weil/Cartier divisor API at scheme generality.

sub-area of algebraic geometry the project has not been using*: the

structurally blind to codim-≥2 points (a DVR is *exactly* a codim-1 local ring; there is

be filled (`ℙ²⇢ℙ¹` at `[0:0:1]`), so the group law is essential there.

  rw [show lift (𝟙 A) (toUnit A ≫ η[A]) ≫ μ[A] ≫ α = α by
        rw [← Category.assoc, lift_comp_one_right, Category.id_comp],

        rw [← Category.assoc, lift_comp_one_left, Category.id_comp]] at key

  exact { one_hom := hα, mul_hom := by rw [key, Hom.mul_def, lift_fst_comp_snd_comp] }

1	\chapter{The Albanese universal property of \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\)}
2	\label{chap:Albanese_AlbaneseUP}
3	% archon:covers AlgebraicJacobian/Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean
4	
5	Let \(k\) be an algebraically closed field, let \(C\) be a smooth proper
6	geometrically irreducible curve over \(k\), and let \(P_0\in C(k)\).  Write
7	\(g\) for the genus of \(C\) and assume \(g>0\).  This chapter proves that
8	the Abel--Jacobi map
9	\[
10	  \iota_{P_0}\colon C\longrightarrow \Pic^0_{C/k}
11	\]
12	is the Albanese morphism of the pointed curve \((C,P_0)\).  The proof uses
13	the canonical map from the \(g\)-th symmetric power of \(C\) to its
14	Jacobian.  In positive characteristic, generic injectivity of this map does
15	not by itself imply birationality: a purely inseparable map may also have
16	one geometric point in its generic fibre.  The differential calculation
17	that excludes this possibility is therefore included explicitly.
18	
19	\section{The Jacobian and the Abel--Jacobi map}
20	\label{sec:albaneseup_setup}
21	
22	The construction of the identity component of the Picard scheme gives
23	\[
24	  J:=\Pic^0_{C/k}.
25	\]
26	It is a group scheme by \cref{thm:pic0_group_structure}, smooth by
27	\cref{thm:pic0_smooth}, proper by \cref{thm:pic0_proper}, and geometrically
28	irreducible by \cref{thm:pic0_geom_irred}.
29	
30	\begin{definition}
31	  [The Abel--Jacobi morphism]
32	  \label{def:abel_jacobi_morphism}
33	  \source{abelian-varieties:page-0107}
34	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Pic0.abelJacobi}
35	  \uses{def:pic_scheme, thm:pic0_group_structure}
36	
37	  The relative degree-zero line bundle associated with the rigidified
38	  diagonal on \(C\times C\) defines a classifying morphism
39	  \(\iota_{P_0}\colon C\to J\), called the \emph{Abel--Jacobi morphism}.
40	\end{definition}
41	
42	\begin{lemma}
43	  [Formula and basepoint of the Abel--Jacobi morphism]
44	  \label{lem:abel_jacobi_morphism}
45	  \source{abelian-varieties:page-0107, abelian-varieties:page-0110}
46	  \uses{def:abel_jacobi_morphism}
47	
48	  There is a regular morphism
49	  \[
50	    \iota_{P_0}\colon C\longrightarrow J,
51	    \qquad Q\longmapsto [\mathcal O_C(Q-P_0)],
52	  \]
53	  and \(\iota_{P_0}(P_0)=0_J\).
54	\end{lemma}
55	
56	\begin{proof}
57	  On \(C\times C\), viewed over the second factor, consider the
58	  rigidified relative degree-zero line bundle represented by
59	  \[
60	    \mathcal O_{C\times C}
61	      (\Delta-P_0\times C-C\times P_0).
62	  \]
63	  Its restriction over \(Q\in C(k)\), modulo a line bundle pulled back
64	  from the base, is \(\mathcal O_C(Q-P_0)\).  The moduli property of
65	  \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) therefore gives the displayed morphism.  At \(Q=P_0\)
66	  the fibre is the trivial line bundle, whose class is the identity of
67	  \(J\).
68	\end{proof}
69	
70	\section{Symmetric powers and their canonical maps}
71	\label{sec:albaneseup_symmetric_powers}
72	
73	\begin{definition}
74	  [Symmetric power of a curve]
75	  \label{def:symmetric_power_curve}
76	  \source{abelian-varieties:page-0100}
77	
78	  For \(r\ge 1\), the \emph{\(r\)-th symmetric power} \(C^{(r)}\) is the
79	  quotient of \(C^r\) by permutation of the factors, with quotient morphism
80	  \(\pi_r\colon C^r\to C^{(r)}\).  Every symmetric morphism from \(C^r\) to a
81	  \(k\)-scheme factors uniquely through \(\pi_r\).
82	\end{definition}
83	
84	\begin{lemma}
85	  [Properties of the symmetric-power projection]
86	  \label{lem:symmetric_power_projection_properties}
87	  \source{abelian-varieties:page-0100}
88	  \uses{def:symmetric_power_curve}
89	
90	  The quotient morphism \(\pi_r\colon C^r\to C^{(r)}\) is finite,
91	  surjective, and separable.
92	\end{lemma}
93	
94	\begin{proof}
95	  On an invariant affine chart the target ring is the ring of
96	  \(S_r\)-invariants.  Every element of the source ring is integral over this
97	  invariant ring, so the quotient is finite; the topological quotient
98	  description gives surjectivity.  Finally, the induced extension of
99	  function fields is the finite invariant-field extension for a group of
100	  automorphisms, and is therefore separable.
101	\end{proof}
102	
103	\begin{definition}
104	  [The symmetric-power carrier]
105	  \label{def:symmetric_power_curve_carrier}
106	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Pic0.SymmetricPower}
107	  \uses{def:symmetric_power_curve}
108	
109	  The underlying \(k\)-scheme of \(C^{(r)}\) is denoted
110	  \(\operatorname{SymmetricPower}(C,r)\).
111	\end{definition}
112	
113	\begin{lemma}
114	  [Nonsingularity of a symmetric power of a curve]
115	  \label{lem:symmetric_power_nonsingular}
116	  \source{abelian-varieties:page-0100}
117	  \uses{def:symmetric_power_curve}
118	
119	  If \(C\) is nonsingular, then \(C^{(r)}\) is nonsingular.
120	\end{lemma}
121	
122	\begin{proof}
123	  At the image of \((Q,\ldots,Q)\), choose a parameter \(X\) at \(Q\).
124	  The completed local ring of \(C^r\) is
125	  \(k[[X_1,\ldots,X_r]]\), and the completed local ring of the quotient is
126	  its invariant subring.  The fundamental theorem on symmetric functions
127	  identifies this with
128	  \(k[[\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r]]\), which is regular.  At a divisor with
129	  several distinct support points, the completed local ring is the
130	  completed tensor product of the corresponding invariant power-series
131	  rings, and is again regular.
132	\end{proof}
133	
134	\begin{definition}
135	  [The symmetric sum morphism]
136	  \label{def:symmetric_product_av_map}
137	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Pic0.symmetricPowerAVMap}
138	  \uses{def:symmetric_power_curve_carrier}
139	
140	  For a morphism \(\varphi\colon C\to A\) to an abelian variety, denote the
141	  induced morphism from the symmetric-power carrier by
142	  \(\varphi^{(r)}\colon C^{(r)}\to A\).
143	\end{definition}
144	
145	\begin{lemma}
146	  [Symmetrisation of a morphism to an abelian variety]
147	  \label{lem:symmetric_product_av_map}
148	  \source{abelian-varieties:page-0110}

219	  \[

221	  \]

223	  differentials that vanish at \(Q\).  Outside the common zero locus of a
224	  basis of this latter space,
225	  adding \(Q\) lowers \(h^1\) by exactly one.  Starting with the zero
226	  divisor, for which \(h^1=g\), and repeating this argument \(r\) times

327	\begin{proposition}
328	  [Differentials on a symmetric power]
329	  \label{prop:symmetric_product_differentials}
330	  \source{abelian-varieties:page-0108, abelian-varieties:page-0109}
331	  \uses{lem:symmetric_product_to_jacobian_formula}
332	
333	  Pullback by \(f^{(r)}\) is an isomorphism
334	  \[
335	    H^0(J,\Omega_J^1)\xrightarrow{\sim}
336	    H^0(C^{(r)},\Omega_{C^{(r)}}^1).
337	  \]
338	  Under the canonical identification of either side with
339	  \(H^0(C,\Omega_C^1)\), the form corresponding to \(\omega\) vanishes at
340	  an effective divisor \(D\) if and only if
341	  \(\operatorname{div}(\omega)\ge D\).
342	\end{proposition}
343	
344	\begin{proof}
345	  \uses{lem:symmetric_power_projection_properties,
346	    lem:abel_jacobi_one_forms}
347	  A global one-form on \(C^r\) is a sum of pullbacks from the factors.
348	  Hence the invariant forms are exactly
349	  \(\sum_i p_i^*\omega\), with \(\omega\in H^0(C,\Omega_C^1)\).
350	  The quotient map \(\pi_r\) is separable, so pullback embeds
351	  \(H^0(C^{(r)},\Omega^1)\) into this invariant subspace.  The composite
352	  \[
353	    H^0(J,\Omega_J^1)\longrightarrow H^0(C^{(r)},\Omega^1)
354	      \longrightarrow H^0(C^r,\Omega^1)^{S_r}
355	  \]
356	  is the pullback by the sum of the \(r\) copies of the Abel--Jacobi map.
357	  By \cref{lem:abel_jacobi_one_forms}, it sends a form to
358	  \(\sum_i p_i^*\omega\) and is an isomorphism.  Consequently both arrows
359	  in the display are isomorphisms.
360	
361	  It remains to identify vanishing at a divisor.  First take \(D=rQ\),
362	  choose a parameter \(X\) at \(Q\), and write
363	  \(\omega=(a_0+a_1X+\cdots)dX\).  In the completed local ring of
364	  \(C^{(r)}\) at \(D\), use the elementary symmetric functions
365	  \(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r\) in local parameters
366	  \(X_1,\ldots,X_r\), and put
367	  \(\tau_j=\sum_iX_i^j\,dX_i\).  The identities
368	  \[
369	    \sigma_m\tau_0-\sigma_{m-1}\tau_1+\cdots+(-1)^m\tau_m
370	      =d\sigma_{m+1}
371	      \qquad(0\le m<r)
372	  \]
373	  show that \(\tau_0,\ldots,\tau_{r-1}\) form a basis of the cotangent
374	  module.  The descended form is \(\sum_{j\ge0}a_j\tau_j\), so it
375	  vanishes at \(D\) exactly when
376	  \(a_0=\cdots=a_{r-1}=0\), equivalently when
377	  \(\operatorname{ord}_Q(\omega)\ge r\).  The same calculation in the
378	  completed local product for
379	  \(D=\sum_Q n_QQ\) gives the stated criterion.
380	\end{proof}

382	\begin{lemma}
383	  [Tangent sequence of the canonical symmetric-power map]
384	  \label{lem:symmetric_product_tangent_exact}
385	  \source{abelian-varieties:page-0107, abelian-varieties:page-0109}
386	  \uses{lem:symmetric_product_to_jacobian_formula}
387	
388	  Let \(F=|D|\) be the fibre of \(f^{(r)}\) through an effective divisor
389	  \(D\), and put \(a=f^{(r)}(D)\).  The sequence
390	  \[
391	    0\longrightarrow T_DF\longrightarrow T_DC^{(r)}
392	      \xrightarrow{\,d f^{(r)}_D\,}T_aJ
393	  \]
394	  is exact.  In particular, if \(h^0(D)=1\), then
395	  \(d f^{(r)}_D\) is injective.
396	\end{lemma}
397	
398	\begin{proof}
399	  \uses{prop:symmetric_product_differentials,
400	    lem:symmetric_power_nonsingular, thm:adelic_serreDuality,
401	    thm:adelic_riemannRoch}
402	  The first arrow is injective because the fibre is a closed subscheme, and
403	  its image lies in the kernel because \(f^{(r)}\) is constant on the
404	  fibre.  By \cref{prop:symmetric_product_differentials}, the annihilator
405	  in \(T_aJ^\vee\) of the image of \(d f^{(r)}_D\) is
406	  \(H^0(C,\Omega_C^1(-D))\).  Serre duality therefore gives
407	  \[
408	    \dim\ker(d f^{(r)}_D)=r-g+h^1(D).
409	  \]
410	  The fibre \(F\) is the projective space of effective divisors in the
411	  complete linear system, so it is smooth of dimension \(h^0(D)-1\).
412	  Thus \(\dim T_DF=\dim|D|=h^0(D)-1\), and Riemann--Roch says
413	  \(h^0(D)-1=r-g+h^1(D)\).  The included subspaces have the same
414	  dimension, proving exactness.  When \(h^0(D)=1\), this dimension is zero.
415	\end{proof}

417	\begin{lemma}
418	  [Birationality of the canonical map]
419	  \label{lem:symmetric_product_to_jacobian}
420	  \source{abelian-varieties:page-0107, abelian-varieties:page-0108,
421	    abelian-varieties:page-0109}
422	  \uses{lem:symmetric_product_to_jacobian_formula}
423	
424	  For \(1\le r\le g\), the morphism
425	  \[
426	    f^{(r)}\colon C^{(r)}\longrightarrow W^r
427	  \]
428	  is birational.  In particular, \(W^g=J\), and
429	  \(f^{(g)}\colon C^{(g)}\to J\) is a birational surjective morphism.
430	\end{lemma}
431	
432	\begin{proof}
433	  \uses{lem:symmetric_power_projection_properties,
434	    lem:symmetric_product_general_divisor,
435	    lem:symmetric_product_tangent_exact, lem:jacobian_dimension,
436	    thm:pic0_geom_irred}
437	  The product \(C^r\) has dimension \(r\), and the finite surjective map
438	  \(C^r\to C^{(r)}\) shows that \(C^{(r)}\) also has dimension \(r\).
439	  By \cref{lem:symmetric_product_general_divisor}, the map is injective on
440	  geometric points over a dense open subset.  It is therefore generically
441	  quasi-finite, so its image \(W^r\) has dimension \(r\).  Thus the induced
442	  extension of function fields has separable degree one.  In positive characteristic
443	  this still leaves open the possibility of a nontrivial purely
444	  inseparable extension.  Choose \(D\) in that open.  Then \(h^0(D)=1\),
445	  so \cref{lem:symmetric_product_tangent_exact} makes
446	  \(d f^{(r)}_D\) injective.  Since source and image both have dimension
447	  \(r\), the differential has full rank, and the function-field extension
448	  is generically separable.  Its inseparable degree is therefore also one.
449	  The function fields of \(C^{(r)}\) and \(W^r\) are equal, proving
450	  birationality.
451	
452	  For \(r=g\), the image \(W^g\) is a closed irreducible subvariety of the
453	  irreducible variety \(J\) and has dimension \(g=\dim J\), the latter
454	  equality being \cref{lem:jacobian_dimension}.  Hence
455	  \(W^g=J\).  Surjectivity follows because \(C^{(g)}\) is proper and its
456	  image is exactly \(W^g\).
457	\end{proof}

471	  \(\varphi\colon C\to A\) be pointed at \(P_0\).  There is a unique

473	  \[

# Analogy: extend a rational map from a smooth projective surface to a proper group scheme without Weil divisors

## Mode
cross-domain-inspiration

## Slug
thm32-extend

## Iteration
164

## Structural problem (abstracted)
Given a morphism defined on a dense open `U ⊆ X` of an integral regular scheme into a
target `Y` whose structure morphism is proper, decide where it extends. Two sub-shapes:
(1) **codim-1 extension** — extend across every height-1 point (the local ring is a
DVR); (2) **emptiness** — fill the remaining codim-≥2 locus, which for a *proper* target
is only possible when extra structure (a group law on `Y`) is present. The blocker is
that the classical emptiness proof (Milne Lemma 3.3) is phrased with Weil divisors, and
Mathlib has no Weil/Cartier divisor API at scheme generality.

## Failed approaches (from directive context)
- Hand-building Weil-divisor theory (`div(f)`, prime divisors) on `ℙ¹×ℙ¹`: Mathlib has
  no usable scheme-level divisor API; building one is out of scope.

## Key finding up front
Mathlib **already ships the entire codim-1 / "Theorem 3.1" half** as a *different
sub-area of algebraic geometry the project has not been using*: the
`AlgebraicGeometry.RationalMap` + `ValuativeCriterion` + `SpreadingOut` stack. The
"defined at every codim-1 point ⟺ complement has codim ≥ 2" statement is **pure
properness, no group, no divisors**, and is fully portable today. The emptiness step
(Lemma 3.3) is genuinely *not* a valuative side-step — the valuative criterion is
structurally blind to codim-≥2 points (a DVR is *exactly* a codim-1 local ring; there is
no "codim-2 valuative criterion"). For a general proper target the codim-2 locus cannot
be filled (`ℙ²⇢ℙ¹` at `[0:0:1]`), so the group law is essential there.

10	/-!
11	# Rational maps to an abelian variety extend
12	
13	Over an algebraically closed field `k̄`, a rational map from a nonsingular
14	variety to an abelian variety extends, uniquely, to a regular morphism
15	(Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §I.3, Theorem 3.2). The argument combines two
16	results of `Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean`: the indeterminacy locus of a
17	rational map from a nonsingular variety to a complete variety has codimension
18	`≥ 2` (Theorem 3.1), while the indeterminacy locus of a rational map into a
19	group variety is empty or of pure codimension `1` (Lemma 3.3). The two
20	conditions are incompatible unless the locus is empty, so `f` is everywhere
21	defined; uniqueness is the agreement principle for morphisms out of a reduced
22	scheme into a separated scheme.
23	
24	The extension theorem is what the Albanese universal property
25	(`Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean`) uses to promote the symmetric-product rational
26	map `C^{(g)} ⇢ A` to a regular morphism `J → A`.
27	
28	## Main results
29	
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.RationalMap.extend_to_av` — for `X` a nonsingular
31	  variety over `k̄` and `A` an abelian variety over `k̄`, every rational map
32	  `f : X ⇢ A` equals `g.toRationalMap` for a unique morphism `g : X ⟶ A`.
33	
34	The pure-codimension-one input, Milne Lemma 3.3
35	(`indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme` in `Albanese/Milne33.lean`), is
36	**proved** as of run 0069, so `extend_to_av` is unconditional and axiom-clean
37	(`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only).
38	
39	## Conventions
40	
41	An **abelian variety over `k̄`** is an object `A : Over (Spec (.of k̄))`
42	carrying:
43	
44	- `[GrpObj A]` (group-object structure on the over-category),
45	- `[IsProper A.hom]` (complete),
46	- `[Smooth A.hom]` (nonsingular),
47	- `[GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]`.
48	
49	A **nonsingular variety over `k̄`** is an object `X : Over (Spec (.of k̄))`
50	carrying:
51	
52	- `[Smooth X.hom]`,
53	- `[GeometricallyIrreducible X.hom]`,
54	- `[IsSeparated X.hom]`,
55	- `[LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom]`,
56	- `[IsIntegral X.left]`,
57	- `[IsReduced X.left]`.
58	
59	## References
60	
61	* Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §I.3, Theorem 3.2, p. 17.

76	/-! ## Rational maps to an abelian variety extend
77	
78	Let `k̄` be an algebraically closed field, `X` a nonsingular variety over `k̄`
79	(smooth, geometrically irreducible, separated, locally of finite type,
80	integral, reduced) and `A` an abelian variety over `k̄` (a group object that is
81	proper, smooth and geometrically irreducible). For every rational map
82	`f : X ⇢ A` there is a unique regular morphism `g : X ⟶ A` whose induced
83	rational map is `f`.
84	
85	Milne's argument: let `U ⊆ X` be a maximal open of definition of `f` and
86	`Z := X ∖ U`. The codimension-`≥ 2` indeterminacy theorem for rational maps
87	into a complete variety gives `codim Z ≥ 2`; the pure-codimension-`1`
88	indeterminacy lemma for maps into a group variety says `Z` is empty or of pure
89	codimension `1`. Both together force `Z = ∅`, so `U = X` and `f` has a regular
90	representative on all of `X`. Uniqueness is the agreement principle
91	`AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isDominant`: two morphisms `X ⟶ A` out of a reduced
92	scheme into a separated scheme that agree on a dense open agree everywhere. -/
93

95	(Stacks `056S`/`033B` over `k̄`). Used to derive `IsReduced A.left` in
96	`av_isIntegral_of_smooth_geomIrred` below.
97	
98	The proof is `isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed` in
99	`Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean`: the stalks are localisations of
100	standard-smooth `k̄`-algebras, whose localisations at maximal ideals are
101	regular local hence domains, and reducedness is checked at those maximal
102	localisations and then transported to the stalks. Algebraic closure of `k̄` is
103	genuinely used. -/
104	private theorem isReduced_of_smooth_over_field
105	    {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
106	    (A : Over (Spec (.of kbar)))
107	    [Smooth A.hom] :
108	    IsReduced A.left :=
109	  isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed A
110	
111	/-- **An abelian variety has integral underlying scheme.** For an abelian
112	variety `A` over an algebraically closed field `k̄` — an object
113	`A : Over (Spec (.of k̄))` carrying
114	`[GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]` —
115	the scheme `A.left` is integral.
116	
117	Three steps:
118	
119	1. `Spec k̄` is a one-point scheme.
120	2. Geometric irreducibility of `A.hom` over a one-point base gives
121	   `IrreducibleSpace A.left`
122	   (`GeometricallyIrreducible.irreducibleSpace_of_subsingleton`).
123	3. Smoothness over the algebraically closed field gives `IsReduced A.left`
124	   (`isReduced_of_smooth_over_field`), and irreducible plus reduced is
125	   integral (`isIntegral_of_irreducibleSpace_of_isReduced`). -/
126	private theorem av_isIntegral_of_smooth_geomIrred
127	    {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
128	    (A : Over (Spec (.of kbar)))
129	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom]
130	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] :
131	    IsIntegral A.left := by
132	  -- Step 1: `Spec k̄` has a unique point (Mathlib instance
133	  -- `Scheme.instUniqueCarrierCarrierCommRingCatSpecOf`); both
134	  -- `Subsingleton` and `Nonempty` follow.
135	  haveI : Subsingleton (Spec (.of kbar) : Scheme.{u}) := inferInstance
136	  haveI : Nonempty (Spec (.of kbar) : Scheme.{u}) := inferInstance
137	  -- Step 2: geometric irreducibility over a singleton base gives `IrreducibleSpace`.
138	  haveI : IrreducibleSpace A.left :=
139	    GeometricallyIrreducible.irreducibleSpace_of_subsingleton A.hom
140	  -- Step 3: smoothness over the algebraically closed base field forces
141	  -- reducedness of the source (`isReduced_of_smooth_over_field`).
142	  haveI : IsReduced A.left := isReduced_of_smooth_over_field A
143	  exact isIntegral_of_irreducibleSpace_of_isReduced A.left
144	
145	/-- **The indeterminacy locus of a rational map to an abelian variety is
146	empty.** For a rational map `f : X ⇢ A` of `k̄`-varieties from a nonsingular
147	variety `X` to an abelian variety `A` over an algebraically closed field `k̄`,
148	`indeterminacyLocus f = ∅`.
149	
150	Two inputs combine (Milne, proof of Theorem 3.2):
151	
152	1. `indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme` (Milne Lemma 3.3): for a
153	   rational map from a smooth integral variety into a *group* variety, the
154	   indeterminacy locus is empty or of pure codimension `1` — every point of
155	   `Z(f)` specialises from a coheight-`1` point *of `Z(f)`*.

157	   rational map from a nonsingular variety into a complete variety, every
158	   point of the indeterminacy locus has coheight `≥ 2`.
159	
160	If `Z(f)` were non-empty, the second disjunct of (1) would produce a point
161	`z ∈ Z(f)` with `coheight z = 1`, contradicting (2). Hence `Z(f) = ∅`.
162	
163	Both inputs need `f` to be a rational map *over `k̄`* (the hypothesis `hover`,
164	Milne's ambient assumption). Note that Milne 3.1 alone is not enough: for a
165	general complete target, codimension-`≥ 2` indeterminacy does not imply an
166	extension (see `existsUnique_hom_of_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty`); the
167	group-variety input (1) is what forces `Z(f) = ∅`.
168

170	so this lemma is unconditional. -/

  have : IsProper G'.hom := by dsimp [G']; infer_instance
  have : IsIntegral (G' ⊗ G').left := by dsimp [G']; infer_instance
  let : GrpObj G' := Functor.grpObjObj
  have := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_isIntegral_tensorObj_of_isAlgClosed G'

  apply (Over.pullback f).map_injective
  rw [← cancel_epi (Functor.Monoidal.μIso (Over.pullback f) G G).hom]
